# Recipe — add a service module (a third-party SDK behind an existing framework port)

A **service module** is an optional, out-of-tree UPM package that implements a port the framework
already has, backed by an external SDK — AppLovin MAX behind `IAdsService` (`pf-ads-max`, the first
one), Firebase behind `IAnalyticsProvider`. Only the SKUs that install it resolve it; every other SKU
keeps the shipped fake and never sees the SDK.

The whole tier reduces to one sentence: **the framework must not know a module exists, and a module
must not know a game exists.** Governing text: the service-modules spine, AD-MOD-1..17 (the tool kind: AD-MOD-14, AD-MOD-15).

## 0. First, prove it is a module

| What you have | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| An **external-SDK implementation of a port that already exists** | This recipe — a module package. |
| Logic with **no external dependency** | Register it in your SKU installer. No module, no package. |
| A **new port**, a new event type, a new `BootCap`, a new RenderLayer, a new migrator, a new `RegisterMessageBroker<T>` | **Spine change** — route it (`AGENTS.framework.md` §7b) *before* the module is written. |
| A fifth assembly role (§2) | **Spine change** — route it. |
| **Editor or command-line capability** (a release build pipeline, an importer, a generator) that borrows **no runtime seam** | A **tool** module — `pf-module/2`, `kind: tool` (§13). |

**A module defines no seam.** It may only implement an existing port, occupy the type-erased installer
slot, and replace an existing boot node's implementation (§6). Adding a module that stays inside those
three is **not** a spine change: it adds no framework assembly, reference edge, RenderLayer, event
type or kernel boot node.

A module is **never** inside `com.classicspins.prototype-framework` (every SKU would inherit the SDK)
and **never** under `Assets/<Sku>/` (it would know a game). It is its own package.

## 1. Know which of the two port shapes you have

| Port | Resolution | `port.mode` |
|---|---|---|
| `IAnalyticsProvider` | `FanOutAnalytics` resolves `IEnumerable<IAnalyticsProvider>` | **`additive`** — N providers coexist. |
| `IAdsService`, `IPurchaseService`, most others | Single resolve | **`replacement`** — yours supersedes the fake. |

Replacement is "register later", never "delete the framework's line": SKU installers run after every
framework installer, and in VContainer the later registration wins a single resolve. The superseded
fake stays registered and is never constructed. `port.mode` is also what Doctor reads: two live
`replacement` modules on one port are a conflict, two `additive` ones are the design.

## 2. The package layout — four roles, one gated

*(The service kind. A tool has only `Editor/` and `Editor/Core/`, both editor-only — §13.)*

```
Packages/com.classicspins.pf-<domain>/
├── package.json            deps: the framework only — NEVER the SDK
├── pf-module.json          the self-description (§3) — the single source of truth
├── Runtime/Core/           ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.<Domain>.Core     engine-free, ungated
├── Runtime/Sdk/            ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.<Domain>.Sdk      gated by PF_<SDK>
├── Runtime/                ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.<Domain>          ungated: installer + Null<Sdk>Bridge
├── Editor/                 ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.<Domain>.Editor   editor-only, ungated, #if inside
└── Tests~/<Module>HeadlessTests/                                            globs Runtime/Core/** only — CI step 5c
```

| Role | Engine | Gated | Holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `….Core` | free (`noEngineReferences: true`) | no | the port implementation, `I<Sdk>Bridge`, the boot node, the preflight **decision** rules — everything hard |
| `….Sdk` | bound | **yes** — the only one | `<Sdk>Bridge`, the thin shell over the SDK. The **only runtime assembly that names an SDK type**. Also the marker type (below) |
| `…` (runtime) | bound | **no, never** | `<Sdk>Installer : ScriptableObject, IInstaller` and `Null<Sdk>Bridge` |
| `….Editor` | editor-only | no (uses `#if PF_<SDK>`) | the `IModulePreflight` implementation and its **fact gathering** (§8). Mandatory for an SDK-bearing module |

A genuinely empty role may be omitted. **Namespace ≡ assembly name**, as everywhere in the framework.

**Allowed references.** Runtime roles: only `ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.{Application, Domain}`,
`VContainer`, `UniTask`, the module's own assemblies and the SDK's runtime assembly. The Editor role
may add `ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Editor` and the SDK's editor-only assembly. **Never**
`Presentation`, `Views`, `Infrastructure`, `Composition`, and never `Game.*`. No SKU assembly ever
references the SDK's runtime assembly — the module is the one path into the SDK.

**The `Sdk` role is the only define-gated assembly**. For a UPM SDK (registry or manually installed
tarball), `versionDefines` arms it, keyed on the SDK package with a minimum-version expression:

```jsonc
// Runtime/Sdk/ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Ads.Max.Sdk.asmdef
{
  "name": "ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Ads.Max.Sdk",
  "references": [ "ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Ads.Max.Core", "UniTask", "MaxSdk.Scripts" ],
  "defineConstraints": [ "PF_MAX" ],
  "versionDefines": [ { "name": "com.applovin.mediation.ads", "expression": "8.0.0", "define": "PF_MAX" } ]
}
```

The ungated runtime and Editor roles carry the **same `versionDefines` entry** (so `#if PF_MAX` works
inside them) and **no** `defineConstraints`. The runtime role references the `Sdk` assembly
unconditionally and names its types only under `#if PF_<SDK>`. That edge is legal only because Unity
**drops** a reference to an assembly whose define constraint is unsatisfied instead of failing the
compile — undocumented; verified in `UnityCsReference` `CustomScriptAssembly.cs:568` →
`EditorBuildRules.cs:244, 451-465`. Cite it wherever your code relies on it.

**The marker.** The `Sdk` role declares one empty type named `PfModuleMarker_<DEFINE>` —
`internal static class PfModuleMarker_PF_MAX { }` — in any namespace. The Wizard and Doctor look it up
by reflection in the module's gated assembly to confirm it actually compiled. A UPM `versionDefines`
symbol never appears in Player Settings. For manual DLL requirements, DLL readiness plus this same
marker determine `define:`, and Doctor also compares the declared symbol for DLL/symbol mismatches.

**SDK distribution has three paths.** Registry SDKs use `requires.dependencies`; local `.tgz` packages
use `requires.manualPackages`; `.unitypackage` SDKs shipping managed DLLs use
`requires.manualAssemblies` (§3a). Loose source imported into `Assembly-CSharp` remains unreferenceable
from an asmdef. For a DLL SDK, set `overrideReferences: true` and list every SDK DLL explicitly in
`Sdk.precompiledReferences`; only the Sdk runtime role reaches those DLLs. Never leave implicit references
to all auto-referenced plugins enabled.

## 3. `pf-module.json` — the module describes itself

At the package root. A service writes schema `pf-module/1` (a new service keeps writing `/1`; a tool is
`pf-module/2` with `kind: tool` — §13); one reader (`ModuleMetadata.Parse`) accepts majors 1 and 2 and
returns a named rejection for a bad file, never a half-read object. `pf-ads-max`'s instance, abridged:

```jsonc
{
  "schema": "pf-module/1",
  "id": "com.classicspins.pf-ads-max",            // == package.json "name" — the drift gate checks it
  "displayName": "Ads — AppLovin MAX",
  "frameworkRange": ">=0.4.0 <0.5.0",              // npm node-semver range, prerelease semantics
  "port": {
    "interface": "ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Application.IAdsService",
    "mode": "replacement",                         // replacement | additive
    "replacesBootNode": "AdsInit"                  // key REQUIRED; null when no boot node is replaced
  },
  "ports": [                                       // OPTIONAL — every SECONDARY port the installer registers
    { "interface": "ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Application.IDevTool", "mode": "additive" },
    { "interface": "ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Application.IAdsPrivacyOptions", "mode": "replacement" }
  ],                                               // never a replacesBootNode key here
  "requires": {                                    // Install writes only registries + dependencies
    "scopedRegistries": [ { "name": "AppLovin MAX Unity", "url": "…", "scopes": [ "com.applovin.mediation.ads", "…" ] } ],
    "dependencies": { "com.applovin.mediation.ads": "8.6.5" }     // EXACT versions, never ranges
  },
  "define": "PF_MAX",                              // the define the Sdk role waits on
  "installer": {
    "type": "ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Ads.Max.MaxAdsInstaller",
    "menu": "PrototypeFramework/Ads/AppLovin MAX Installer",
    "assetPath": "Assets/{sku}/Installers/MaxAdsInstaller.asset"  // {sku} substituted at install
  },
  "manualSteps": [ "AppLovin ▸ Integration Manager → paste the SDK Key", "…" ],   // human zone, shown verbatim
  "docs": "recipes/add-service-module.md"
}
```

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `schema`, `id`, `displayName`, `frameworkRange`, `port`, `requires`, `define`, `installer` | **Required** (service). `summary`, `source`, `manualSteps`, `docs`, `ports` are optional. A `/2` service adds `kind: "service"`. |
| `requires.dependencies` | **Exact pins.** A floating SDK silently changes what the bridge was written against. |
| `frameworkRange` | The one range in the file. UPM treats a dependency version as a minimum and never fails on a breaking framework bump — this is what names it. Advisory while the framework is dev-linked or embedded. |
| `port.mode` | The only field that decides conflict (`replacement`) versus fan-out (`additive`). |
| `ports[]` | Every **secondary** port the module registers, as `{ "interface": "…", "mode": "replacement" \| "additive" }` — e.g. a replacement of a framework `Null*` port, or one more additive registration. `port` stays the primary seam and the **only** carrier of `replacesBootNode`: the key must be absent from a `ports[]` entry — present at all, even `null`, it is refused (`ports[0].replacesBootNode`). The `seam:` fact and `modules --check` read `port` ∪ `ports[]` alike — two modules declaring one interface where either says `replacement` is `seam:`, and Install is refused. Declare **every** port your installer registers: an undeclared one is a clash that surfaces only at runtime, and it is held by review, not by any gate (AD-MOD-4). Schema stays `pf-module/1`. |
| `define` | Matches the `Sdk` `defineConstraints` and marker suffix. UPM SDKs arm it with `versionDefines`; manual DLL SDKs use only framework `ModuleDefineSync`, with no module-symbol `versionDefines`. |
| `installer.type` | A class in that namespace, implementing `IInstaller`, compiled by the **ungated** runtime role. |
| `installer.menu` | The installer's `[CreateAssetMenu]` `menuName`, verbatim. The Wizard, checklist and Doctor show it as `Assets ▸ Create ▸ …` — it is never a top-level menu. |
| `manualSteps` | Everything in the human zone (rule #12): SDK keys, network selection, the installer-asset drop. Displayed, **never performed**. |

`package.json` depends on the framework only. The SDK is declared in `requires`. Install applies only
registry requirements to the consumer manifest; manual requirements remain checklist work. This keeps
SKU #0 SDK-free.

## 3a. Manual SDK requirements and recovery (framework >=0.9.0)

Both arrays are optional and default empty. DLL pins must be plain `X.Y.Z` (no prerelease/build suffix,
since managed AssemblyVersion cannot compare those); package pins keep the existing exact SemVer policy.
Bad arrays, filenames/package ids,
missing fields, duplicate entries and non-exact versions receive rejections naming the indexed field.
A tool must keep both arrays empty, as with its other requirements.

```jsonc
"requires": {
  "scopedRegistries": [],
  "dependencies": {},
  "manualPackages": [
    { "package": "com.google.firebase.app", "version": "14.1.0" },
    { "package": "com.google.firebase.analytics", "version": "14.1.0" }
  ]
}
// Or, for a DLL-only SDK with no UPM package:
"manualAssemblies": [ { "assembly": "Facebook.Unity.dll", "version": "18.1.1" } ]
```

1. For each manual package, download the named `.tgz`, commit it inside the project (Git LFS recommended),
   then manually add its project-relative `file:` dependency in `Packages/manifest.json`. For example,
   a tarball committed at `Packages/ManualSdk/com.google.firebase.app-14.1.0.tgz` uses the manifest value
   `file:ManualSdk/com.google.firebase.app-14.1.0.tgz` (UPM resolves it relative to `Packages/`). Never use
   an absolute path or an external checkout: CI must resolve the same committed tarball. State accepts
   any resolved source at or above the declared version, and package `versionDefines` still arms the symbol.
2. For each manual assembly, import the vendor `.unitypackage` through `Assets > Import Package >
   Custom Package` into `Assets/`. Name the **tested vendor release and download destination** in
   `manualSteps`. The assembly pin uses inspected managed `AssemblyVersion`, not an archive label:
   the owner-supplied Facebook SDK release 18.1.1 DLLs report **18.1.1.0**. The reader compares on-disk
   `AssemblyName.GetAssemblyName(path).Version`; inactive-platform DLLs need not be loaded, and deleted
   DLLs can remain loaded. Valid DLLs with absent/zero version are **presence-only**; name the tested
   vendor release in the checklist because automatic version assurance is unavailable there.
3. Declare the DLL in `Sdk.precompiledReferences`, set `overrideReferences: true`, keep
   `defineConstraints: ["<declared symbol>"]`, and remove `versionDefines` arming that symbol from every
   role. Manual assemblies and a `versionDefines`-armed module symbol are mutually exclusive.
   `ModuleDefineSync` adds only the declared symbol after reload when every DLL requirement holds,
   across installed NamedBuildTargets; it preserves all undeclared symbols and writes only changed sets.
   Disk presence is insufficient: a declared DLL must have an imported managed PluginImporter enabled for
   **Editor and every installed concrete player target**. This deliberately refuses platform-restricted
   DLL requirements rather than arming a bridge that cannot compile; metadata remains inspectable even
   when the DLL is unavailable to that compiler. Doctor names unavailable compiler input. No AppDomain
   assembly loading is used for presence/version evidence.
   A symbol cannot be shared between manual-DLL and registry-armed modules; synchronization refuses the
   mixed ownership. Shared manual symbols require every declaring module's DLLs, and `define:` names
   any blocking manual peer. It never writes in batchmode or installs an SDK.
4. Delete SDK DLLs/folders **through the Editor**. A framework `AssetModificationProcessor` pre-delete
   hook removes affected symbols synchronously before compilation, including folder deletions. The same
   protection runs before renames/moves that lose a required filename or compiler availability (for example
   an ignored or Editor-only folder); moves preserving compiler availability leave symbols unchanged.
   If discovery or clearing an affected symbol fails, the Editor refuses the deletion/move and names the
   failure. Normal reconciliation isolates unreadable packages and names each one, so unrelated valid
   modules can still synchronize. The `AssetPostprocessor` schedules reconciliation after import/reload:
   it alone is too late because Unity compiles code assets before asset postprocessing.
5. **Safe Mode recovery:** after a branch switch or out-of-Editor SDK deletion, remove the module's
   declared symbol in **Player Settings > Scripting Define Symbols for every installed target**, then
   restore/import the SDK. Project code does not run in Safe Mode and cannot repair this case. Doctor
   reports symbol/DLL mismatches when it can run; the checklist remains accessible while the SDK is absent.

Install never downloads/imports the SDK or writes manual package entries. The numbered checklist remains
available for manual modules while registry work proceeds and after that work completes, including on a
fresh editor session. Read-only recovery instructions remain accessible even when a range/conflict/seam
refuses Install; a blocked job reports the refusal, never completion. Registry work completes before an
unblocked job auto-opens the checklist.

## 4. Absence refuses — it never falls back to the fake

The installer assembly is **never gated**. It always registers your port implementation; only the
bridge behind it depends on the define:

```csharp
private static IMaxBridge CreateBridge(ILog log)
{
#if PF_MAX   // an #if edge into the gated Sdk role — cite UnityCsReference (§2)
    return new ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Ads.Max.Sdk.MaxBridge();
#else
    return new NullMaxBridge(log);
#endif
}
```

`Null<Sdk>Bridge` **fails every call as a result, never a throw, and logs the module id** on each
refusal. It must never leave the framework's fake resolved: `FakeAdsService` **auto-rewards**, so
"falling back" would ship free rewards to every player behind one warning line. A gated installer is
equally wrong — the Master-Scene installer asset becomes a missing script and the fake is back.

## 5. The shipped fake is the specification

**Read the implementation you are replacing before you write yours.** Ports carry contracts the
interface does not state, and the fake is where they are written down. Known ones:

| Port | What the interface does not tell you |
|---|---|
| `IAdsService` | Must publish `AdVisibilityChanged` at show-start **and** show-end, the latter in a `finally` so a cancelled/failed show never strands the four subscribers (audio duck, interaction lock, gameplay tick, banner reflow). **One visibility state per ads module (AD-MOD-12):** every surface that can put SDK UI on screen (a show, the consent flow in `AdsInit`, a privacy-options window) holds **its own slot** in one Core singleton injected into every producer; a producer opens and closes only its own slot, closing it in a `finally`; the fact is **derived** from the open slots (`FullscreenAdVisible` = any fullscreen slot open) and published only when it changes, and no producer constructs it — so the first surface to close never releases the lock under one still on screen. A banner producer (none exists yet) publishes `BannerHeightPx` in **Unity `Screen` pixels**, converting the SDK's dp/pt in its bridge; the reflow's screen→canvas conversion is still owed in `AdBannerReflowSubscriber` and must land before any visible banner. A second fullscreen `ShowAsync` while any fullscreen slot is open is **refused** (`AdResult.Failed`) before it publishes anything or calls the SDK. `FakeAdsService` holds no slots and refuses nothing (it publishes the pair per show), so for visibility the fake is **not** the specification — `pf-ads-max`'s `MaxAdVisibility` is the reference. Must auto-log the outcome via `AdAnalyticsMapping` → `IAnalytics`. `IsReadyAsync` is awaited by `AdsInit` as a readiness probe. Paid impressions go to analytics as **one `AdRevenuePaid` per impression**, tracked from the module's impl layer through `IAnalytics.Track` whatever the consent state (the sink applies consent); it is an analytics record, never a MessagePipe fact, and its parameters are never renamed, retyped, removed or reordered (new ones are appended at the end). `FakeAdsService` deliberately emits **no** revenue, so here the fake is not the specification — `pf-ads-max`'s `MaxRevenueReporter` is the reference. **Readiness is pushed as well as pulled (AD-MOD-11):** publish `AdReadinessChanged(Placement, Ready)` through `IAdReadinessChangedPublisher` (the broker is `AdsInstaller`'s; never register the `Null` twin) from **one** Core readiness state that owns placement→unit bindings and the one `ready(unit)` function — initialized ∧ requested ∧ not being shown ∧ the SDK's loaded read — which answers both `IsReadyAsync` and the push. `Preload` / `IsReadyAsync` / `ShowAsync` bind a placement whether or not the SDK is initialized; a new binding's baseline is never published; load, load-fail, show-start, show-end and a config change publish only a changed value, per unit, to **every** placement bound to it; init completion publishes the settled value for every bound placement (`false` after a failed init). `IsReadyAsync` never publishes. `FakeAdsService` publishes **no** readiness (legal — "no fact yet" means "ask"), so here too the fake is not the specification — `pf-ads-max`'s `MaxAdReadiness` is the reference. |
| `IAnalyticsProvider` | Must never throw, and owns its own retry (an offline backend is yours to queue and retry). `FanOutAnalytics` keeps a per-provider catch only as a safety net: a throw is logged as a **provider defect** naming the event type, and that event is **lost for that provider — never re-sent**. Each event reaches each provider at most once. **Money is counted only from `AdRevenuePaid`** — a provider never synthesizes revenue from `AdShown` / `AdRewarded`, and at most one provider sends revenue to a given backend. |
| `IPurchaseService` | Grants route through the shipped interpreter; a module must not grant directly. |

If you break one of these, nothing fails loudly — the symptom shows up somewhere else entirely.

**Split the SDK boundary.** `I<Sdk>Bridge` (in `Core`) speaks **primitives only** — no SDK type
crosses it. The state machine (load, show, result mapping, publish ordering) lives in `Core` and runs
under `dotnet test` with a fake bridge; `<Sdk>Bridge` in `Sdk` is thin enough to review by eye, and
nothing else covers it.

**Time and platform are injected, never read in `Core`.** `Core` is `noEngineReferences`: no
`Time.*`, no `UniTask.Delay`, no `#if UNITY_*`. A retry or a timeout takes a
`Func<TimeSpan, CancellationToken, UniTask>` delay, which the installer fills with a **realtime**
`UniTask.Delay` (the game may pause `timeScale` while an ad is up); a platform-dependent choice takes a
token the installer maps from `UNITY_ANDROID` / `UNITY_IOS`. The fake delay in the module's tests then
drives every clock by hand.

**Worked example — `pf-ads-max`'s config surface** (all read through `IGameConfig`; the pre-v2 keys
keep working unchanged):

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ads.<P>.rewarded` (int) | non-zero ⇒ placement `P` is rewarded; absent ⇒ interstitial (the framework's own ad-gate key) |
| `ads.max.<X>.<P>.unitId` → `ads.max.<P>.unitId` → `ads.max.<X>.<F>.unitId` → `ads.max.<F>.unitId` | the unit lookup, first non-empty wins; `X` ∈ `android`/`ios` (skipped off-mobile), `F` ∈ `rewarded`/`interstitial` |
| `ads.max.displayTimeoutSeconds` (int) | gap allowed between `Show` and a display signal; absent or ≤ 0 ⇒ 10 |
| `ads.max.autoLog` (int) | absent ⇒ every result is auto-logged; `0` ⇒ none |
| `ads.max.revenueLog` (int) | absent ⇒ every paid impression is tracked as one `AdRevenuePaid`; `0` ⇒ none. Independent of `ads.max.autoLog` |
| `ads.max.verboseLogging` (int) · `ads.max.testDeviceIds` (comma list) | dev knobs applied once before SDK init; absent ⇒ no SDK call |
| `ads.max.devTools` (int) | absent ⇒ the Mediation and Creative Debuggers (`IDevTool`) are available once the SDK is initialized; `0` ⇒ both read unavailable. Read on every `IsAvailable` / `Open` call; a throwing read means off |

After init the format defaults auto-load; a placement's own unit loads once it is requested (`Preload`,
or the first `IsReadyAsync` / `ShowAsync`, which answer not-ready for an unrequested unit). A request
made **before** init — any of the three binds the placement and requests its unit whether or not the SDK
is up — is recorded and loaded when auto-load starts, and init completion then publishes that
placement's settled `AdReadinessChanged`. A failed
load of a requested unit retries after `2^min(attempt, 6)` s; a load success resets the count. The
display timeout covers only `Show` → displayed: **once displayed, a Hidden that never arrives means the
show never returns**, and a timed-out show the SDK displays later covers the screen with no visibility
fact. Both are known, unfixed gaps.

### Consuming readiness in a SKU — `AdReadinessChanged` (AD-MOD-11)

A rewarded offer lights and dims with fill without polling. Five rules, each a review rejection:

1. **Subscribe first** — the plain `ISubscriber<AdReadinessChanged>`, filtered to your placement.
2. **Then call `IsReadyAsync(p)` once.** The subscriber has no replay, so the pull fills the gap before
   the first fact; never poll it afterwards.
3. **"No fact yet" means "ask", never "not ready".** An implementation that never publishes is legal —
   the framework's `FakeAdsService` is one — so the pull is the answer until a fact arrives.
4. **`IBufferedSubscriber<AdReadinessChanged>` is a defect.** It replays a `default` fact (placement
   `null`, `Ready = false`) and holds one value across every placement.
5. **Ready is not may-show.** Offer only while the latest `Ready` for `p` **and** `IAdGate.CanShow(p)`
   are both true; the gate publishes nothing, so re-check it when the offer is drawn. Held by
   `AdReadinessChangedTests.An_offer_is_hidden_for_a_remove_ads_owner_on_an_interstitial_placement_even_when_ready`.

### Developer tools — `IDevTool` (AD-MOD-13)

An SDK's own debugger UI (MAX's Mediation and Creative Debuggers, a Firebase DebugView, an Adjust test
menu) reaches the SKU through the framework port `IDevTool` (`Runtime/Application/Diagnostics/`):
`string Id`, `bool IsAvailable`, `bool Open()`. The framework registers **none** — on the fake the
collection is empty, and that is normal.

**Module side.**

1. **One distinct implementation type per tool**, each a Singleton factory `.As<IDevTool>()` from the
   installer, outside any `#if`. Two Singletons sharing one implementation type make VContainer's
   collection provider throw (DW-35), and `RegisterInstance` is never the answer.
2. **`Id` is `<module-slug>.<tool>`** — `ads-max.mediation-debugger`, `ads-max.creative-debugger` —
   stable and unique in the process. No display string on the port.
3. **Read availability at call time.** `IsAvailable` and `Open` each read the SDK's initialized state
   and any kill switch (`ads.max.devTools`, absent ⇒ on, `0` ⇒ off) on every call — never in a
   constructor or the installer, because config arrives only with `ConfigAvailable`.
4. **`Open` never throws.** Unavailable ⇒ `false`, no SDK call, one warning naming the module and the
   reason. A throwing config read means **off**; a throwing SDK call is a warning and `false`.
5. **Declare it** in `pf-module.json` `ports[]` as `{ "interface": "ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Application.IDevTool", "mode": "additive" }`.
   The SDK call itself is one more primitives-only bridge method.

**SKU side.**

1. Inject `IReadOnlyList<IDevTool>` (or `IEnumerable<IDevTool>`) into the debug menu and list every tool.
2. Map each `Id` to a `LocKey` for its label (rule #4) — never print the id.
3. **Which builds expose tools is the SKU's decision** (a dev flavour define, a hidden gesture). The
   module registers its tools unconditionally; its kill switch is for a SKU that wants them gone from a
   release build's config.
4. An empty list is normal (the framework's fake, or no module installed) — draw the empty state.
5. **No reflection on SDK types** to reach a debugger. If a module lacks the tool you need, add it to
   the module.

### Privacy settings — `IAdsPrivacyOptions` (AD-MOD-9)

A player who wants to withdraw or change personalized-ads consent reaches the **SDK's own consent
form** through the framework port `IAdsPrivacyOptions` (`Runtime/Application/Ads/`): `bool IsAvailable`,
`UniTask<bool> ShowAsync(CancellationToken)`. `ShowAsync` **never throws**: `true` when the form was
shown and completed, `false` when unavailable, refused or failed. `AdsInstaller` registers
`NullAdsPrivacyOptions` (never available, `ShowAsync` false) — the framework owns no consent form.

**Module side** (an ads module whose SDK owns personalized-ads consent).

1. **Replace the Null**: one Singleton factory `.As<IAdsPrivacyOptions>()` from the installer, outside
   any `#if`, never `RegisterInstance`; declare it in `ports[]` as
   `{ "interface": "ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Application.IAdsPrivacyOptions", "mode": "replacement" }`.
2. **Available = initialized ∧ the SDK reports a supported CMP**, both read on every call. The SDK
   calls are two primitives-only bridge members (`pf-ads-max`: `HasSupportedCmp`,
   `ShowCmpForExistingUser(Action<string>)` — `null` on success, else the error text). Neither is a
   consent setter, and neither name contains "Consent".
3. **Refuse, in order, each with one warning naming the module** and no SDK call: a cancelled token; a
   call already running (MAX keeps **one** static completion callback — a second show would overwrite
   the first's); any fullscreen slot open; unavailable; the exclusive slot open refused.
4. **Hold the module's own privacy-options slot** in the one visibility state (AD-MOD-12) from before
   the SDK call until its completion callback, closed in a `finally` — so input, audio and the tick
   gate hold while the form covers the screen, and every ad show is refused meanwhile.
5. **Ignore the token once the form is up, and add no timeout** — the form is human-paced, and
   returning while it still covers the screen desyncs visibility. A synchronous or doubled callback
   never throws; the first value wins.
6. **Write nothing back.** The SDK stores and applies the outcome; never inject `IConsentService`,
   never call `ChangeConsent` (it would rerun `AdsInit`). `pf-ads-max`'s `MaxAdsPrivacyOptions` is the
   reference.

**SKU side.**

1. **Consume the port behind your own interface** (a Presentation-side `IPrivacySettingsRow` port your
   settings controller calls, say) and draw the "Privacy settings" row only while `IsAvailable` — read
   it when the screen opens, never cache it across sessions.
2. **Never register `IAdsPrivacyOptions` yourself.** The SKU installer runs last, so a SKU registration
   wins the resolve and silently shadows the module's — the row would open nothing on device.
3. **An EEA/UK launch precondition.** A SKU that serves the EEA or the UK ships this row; it is
   review-held, no gate checks it. On the framework's Null the row simply never draws.
4. Treat `false` as "nothing changed" — no error dialog for a refusal; the module has already logged
   why.

## 5a. Analytics properties, consent and provider commands (AD-MOD-16/17)

`IAnalytics.SetUserProperty(UserPropKey key, string value)` and
`IAnalyticsProvider.SetUserProperty(UserPropKey key, string value)` share a hand-written Domain
value type, `readonly record struct UserPropKey(string Value)`. It is **not generated**: no manifest
or codegen step. Framework `UserProps.TotalCoins`, `BestStreak` and `MatchesWon` carry `total_coins`,
`best_streak` and `matches_won`. A SKU extends the vocabulary in its own Domain static class:

```csharp
public static class SkuUserProps
{
    public static readonly UserPropKey HighestLevel = new("highest_level");
}
// In a SKU Application service, with IAnalytics injected:
// analytics.SetUserProperty(SkuUserProps.HighestLevel, "42");
```

The one Application `UserPropKeyValidator` enforces `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,23}$`.
`FanOutAnalytics` drops invalid/default names and warns once per name; it forwards valid keys and
string values unchanged to every provider under granted Analytics consent. Properties are never
buffered. A backend with no property API ignores them, warns once per key and documents that choice;
never turn a user property into event parameters.

**Every provider implements `OnAnalyticsConsent(bool granted)` without throwing.** The fan-out
observes consent on every Track, property and Flush call, notifying all providers **before dispatch**
on the first resolved observation and each granted ↔ denied transition. Unresolved alone sends no
notification. One provider's callback defect is logged and does not starve another. On false, stop
native collection and drop the provider's held queue; on true, re-enable collection if already
started. The callback never starts an SDK. Start lazily on a consent-gated send/property/ordinary
command; provider wrappers must forward the consent callback too. Keep native collection off before
that start, including native launch-time auto-collection. Own retry and startup failure locally;
never make analytics SDK startup a new/replacement boot node.

**Provider-specific calls use the shared `IAnalyticsCommands` port.** `AnalyticsInstaller` registers
one singleton `AnalyticsCommandRouter`, collecting every `IAnalyticsCommandTarget` (an empty set is
valid). A provider exposes a unique ordinal `ProviderId`, its module slug such as
`analytics-firebase`, and declares `IAnalyticsCommandTarget` additive in `ports[]`. Register the same
provider instance through both interfaces:

```csharp
builder.Register<MyAnalyticsProvider>(Lifetime.Singleton)
    .As<IAnalyticsProvider, IAnalyticsCommandTarget>();
```

A SKU Application/Composition service or forwarder calls:
`bool Execute(string providerId, string command, IReadOnlyList<KeyValuePair<string, string>> args)`.
Never call it from a View or Model. Every command is synchronous, **main-thread** and no-throw.
The **router never buffers or replays** commands. Ordinary commands require resolved, granted Analytics consent;
otherwise false is returned and logged. A command in the ordinal **`privacy.` namespace** bypasses
consent, but the target must **never start an SDK** for it: act on a started SDK or pre-start API, or
return false. The router logs target exceptions as provider defects and returns false. An unknown
provider is false, warned once per id; duplicate ids warn once on the first command and the first
registered target wins.

**True means accepted:** applied now, or queued until the SDK starts. A target may snapshot and
hold accepted work during startup; it must drop that held work on consent withdrawal.
**False means refused:** an
unknown command, malformed argument, unsupported backend operation or blocked consent. Every
provider README documents the common vocabulary **`set_user_id`** (argument **`id`**) and
**`privacy.forget_me`**, explicitly documenting any unsupported form as false; provider-specific
commands go in that README too. A fact intended for every backend stays a typed `GameEvent`, not a
command. No module/SDK reference is needed in the SKU.

## 6. Replacing a boot node — `BootNodeOverride.Replace`

SDK init that must be awaited, can fail meaningfully or needs ordering is tier 2 — but a module never
adds a kernel node. It **replaces** the framework's, from its installer:

```csharp
builder.Register<MaxAdsInitNode>(r => new MaxAdsInitNode(r.Resolve<IMaxBridge>(), …), Lifetime.Singleton);
builder.Register<BootNodeOverride>(
    r => BootNodeOverride.Replace("AdsInit", r.Resolve<MaxAdsInitNode>()), Lifetime.Transient);
```

- **`Id` and `Provides` identical** to the node replaced. A cap that loses its sole provider makes
  `RunUntilAsync` / `RerunFromAsync` complete silently without ever becoming ready.
- **`Required => false`.** A dead SDK never blocks boot or raises an error screen.
- **Register the node as itself, never as `IBootNode`** — that would put a second `AdsInit` in the graph.
- The override is **`Transient`**: VContainer's collection provider rejects a second Singleton
  `BootNodeOverride`; the node inside it is still the singleton above.
- **Two modules may not replace the same node** — a second override for one target is a composition
  error (Doctor names it as the `seam:` fact before Install).
- `port.replacesBootNode` in `pf-module.json` names the target.

> **`Id` and `Provides` are enforced; `Required` is not.** `BootGraph.Reconcile` throws a
> `BootGraphException` naming the target when a `Replace` changes the target's `Id` or its `Provides`
> set. `Required => false` is a module rule that the framework does not check, because a SKU may
> legitimately replace a `Required` node such as `FirstScene`. The module's own headless tests still
> pin `Required`, along with `Id` and `Provides`, so the module fails in its own gate rather than at
> the consumer's boot.

### Holding a module's node until the game is ready — `Gate` (SKU only)

A SKU whose FTUE must finish before MAX's init, UMP or ATT prompts appear does **not** write a wrapper
node (it would clash with the module's own `Replace("AdsInit", …)` — one `Replace` per target). It adds
a **gate** from its own installer:

```csharp
// Game.Composition — the SKU's installer, never the module's.
builder.Register<BootNodeOverride>(
    r => { var ftue = r.Resolve<IFtueProgress>();
           return BootNodeOverride.Gate("AdsInit", _ => ftue.IsComplete, FtueCaps.FtueLoaded); },
    Lifetime.Transient);

// Later, at a scene/dialog boundary once the FTUE is done:
await bootFlow.RerunFromAsync(BootCaps.AdsReady, ct);
```

`BootGraph.Reconcile` applies the module's `Replace` first, then folds every gate on that target into
one `GatedBootNode`: `Requires` = the node's caps ∪ every gate's extras, `Predicate` = the node's own
AND every gate. A node a gate skips still emits its `Provides` (as `Skipped`). The gate guards the
node's **first entry only** — once its body has run (any result but `Skipped`), reruns ignore the gate.
`Reconcile` throws on a gate whose target is unknown or removed, and on an extra cap that nothing
provides, that is excused, or that the target itself provides. The four rules:

1. **`Gate` is SKU composition only.** A module never registers one — the module does not know a game
   exists, so it cannot know what the game is waiting for.
2. **Every override is a `Transient` factory, never `RegisterInstance`**, until DW-35 lands: VContainer's
   collection provider rejects a second Singleton `BootNodeOverride`, and the module's own `Replace` is
   already in that collection.
3. **Reopen with `RerunFromAsync(<a cap the node provides>)`** — `AdsReady` for `AdsInit` — at a scene or
   dialog boundary. Never rerun from `ConsentResolved` (that reruns the consent node and everything
   behind it), and never from a tick. Reruns are **serialized first come first served**, so this call
   and the consent driver's never interleave; cancelling a queued call's token removes it from the queue.
   So an awaited rerun may first wait for the running one (e.g. the consent driver's) to finish; a
   cancelled queued call throws `OperationCanceledException`, which the caller catches; and never await
   a rerun from inside a boot node — it waits behind itself.
4. **A gate predicate reads only what the node's final `Requires` assert** (the race rule, §4 of
   `AGENTS.framework.md`). Declare the cap that makes your flag readable as an extra; a flag no cap
   asserts can be read before it is loaded.

A throwing gate reads as `false` with one warning on a non-`Required` node, and fails the node (the
reason names the gate) on a `Required` one. A **false** gate reports `Skipped` even on a `Required`
node, and boot carries on with its `Provides` marked `Skipped` — so gate a `Required` node only when every
dependent reads the cap's status, never just its presence.

## 7. Consent — an ads module's SDK owns personalized-ads consent (AD-MOD-9)

Personalized-ads consent is asked, stored and applied by the **SDK's own consent flow**, run inside
the replacement `AdsInit`. `IConsentService` is never its authority.

- The node **does not inject `IConsentService`**; the bridge has **no consent setter**; nothing is
  **written back** (`ChangeConsent` would rerun `AdsInit`).
- It keeps `Requires` on `ConsentResolved`, so the SDK's prompt follows the SKU's own agree gate.
- **No timeout over the interactive flow** — `HardTimeout` must not cut off a player reading a privacy
  prompt. Only non-interactive SDK work may carry an internal timeout.
- Publish `AdVisibilityChanged(true, …)` before the flow and `(false, …)` in a `finally`, so the audio
  duck, interaction lock and tick gate hold while it is on screen — no new subscriber. Do it through
  the module's **one visibility state** (AD-MOD-12): the node opens its own consent-flow slot (never
  refused — SDK init is memoized) and closes it in the `finally`; the state derives the fact and
  publishes it only on change, so the flow ending under a show still up releases nothing.
- **Rerun-idempotent:** SDK init and the consent flow run **at most once per process**; a later
  `RunAsync` returns the memoized outcome (process lifetime, never UserData). Can-show keys on the
  bridge's own initialized state, never `IBootStatus`.
- Configuring the SDK's flow (e.g. MAX's Integration Manager) is a `manualSteps` entry.
- **One consent UI per region.** In GDPR regions the SDK's form (Google UMP behind MAX's CMP) is the
  **only** consent form, for any purpose — a SKU never draws its own consent dialog beside it. A SKU
  agree gate (a ToS/age screen feeding `ConsentResolved`) is not a consent form.
- **ATT is raised only by the SDK flow.** A SKU never calls the iOS App Tracking Transparency prompt
  itself; MAX's flow raises it when configured, inside `AdsInit`.
- **Declare `FrameworkSettings.ServesNoConsentRegion`** honestly (default `false`). `true` resolves
  first-boot consent with `Analytics` granted for a SKU that serves no consent-required region; `false`
  resolves it with nothing granted until a gate scene grants it. `PersonalizedAds` is never granted by
  the framework on either path.
- **"Change privacy settings" is an EEA/UK launch precondition.** The player must be able to reopen the
  SDK's form: the module fills `IAdsPrivacyOptions` (§5), the SKU draws the row. Review-held.

## 8. The build refuses a half-wired install — `IModulePreflight`

**A module — either kind — ships no build preprocessor.** The build-callback list is **closed**
(AD-MOD-6). **Forbidden**: `IPreprocessBuildWithReport`, `IPreprocessBuildWithContext`,
`IPreprocessBuild`, `BuildPlayerProcessor`, `IProcessScene*` / `[PostProcessScene]`,
`IFilterBuildAssemblies`, `IPostBuildPlayerScriptDLLs`, `IUnityLinkerProcessor`, `IPreprocessShaders`,
`IPreprocessComputeShaders`, the legacy `IPostprocessBuild` — the `buildhook` grep in
`sh Tools/CI/greps.sh source` fails each in a module package (and `IPreprocessBuildWithReport` anywhere
first-party outside the framework's own `Editor/`), and that grep is the policy's only home (no per-module copy).
**Permitted** in a module's Editor role: `IPostprocessBuildWithReport`, `[PostProcessBuild]`,
`IPostGenerateGradleAndroidProject`, `AndroidProjectFilesModifier` — each with an explicit order,
transform-only (an `Info.plist` key, a Gradle property), **never overwriting** a different existing value
(log the module, the key and both values; keep the existing one), and never failing a build for a policy
reason. Policy enters through the framework's editor interface instead:

```csharp
// ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Editor.Modules (CS.PF.Editor)
public interface IModulePreflight
{
    string ModuleId { get; }                                          // the pf-module.json id
    IEnumerable<ModulePreflightProblem> Check(BuildTarget target);   // empty == fine
}
```

- The framework's **one** `ModulePreflightBuildHook` discovers every implementation by reflection and
  fails the build with **one** `BuildFailedException` listing every problem, each line prefixed with its
  module id. In an interactive editor a dialog offers each problem's fix action first; under
  `-batchmode` only the throw exists (`DisplayDialog` logs `Canceling DisplayDialog` on 6000.3.12f1),
  so **the throw is the enforcement**.
- **Decisions in `Core`** (`<Module>PreflightRules`, headless-tested row by row); **fact gathering in
  `Editor`** (`BuildTarget`, the SDK's editor-only settings). Call a third-party resolver by
  **reflection only**, so the module compiles where it is not installed.
- **Mandatory for an SDK-bearing module**, optional for a tool. In a consumer this throw is the only
  enforcement that crosses into their build — everything else there is advisory.

## 9. Constructor rule

**No defaulted parameters on a container-resolved constructor.** VContainer ignores C# default values
and resolves every parameter, so `ILog log = null` is not "optional" — it is a hard dependency that
happens to be satisfied. Take the parameters and null-check them.

## 10. Installing it in a SKU — `Framework/Setup Wizard ▸ Modules`

The Wizard applies registry requirements from the file. Manual SDK entries follow §3a:

1. **Bring the module package in** — three doors. Each adds **only the module package** (one
   `Client.AddAndRemove`) and ends; after the reload the module is a discovered row, `Partial`, with
   none of its `requires` applied. None ever chains into Install.
   - **Add an offer** — with the framework **dev-linked** (its manifest entry is `file:…` ending in
     `Packages/com.classicspins.prototype-framework`), every folder beside it in that checkout's
     `Packages/` that holds a `pf-module.json` and is not yet registered is listed under **Offered from
     the linked checkout**. **Add** (behind a confirm naming the entry) writes one manifest entry: the
     framework's own entry text with exactly that suffix swapped for `Packages/<dir>` — relative stays
     relative, and the prefix before the swapped span keeps its separators as written. The framework's
     own entry is never written. A module whose `package.json` is missing, has no `name`, or whose
     `name` ≠ its `id`, or whose `pf-module.json` is invalid is listed with its rejections and **no
     Add**; so is a module the manifest already declares (say a git URL that never resolved) — it is not
     offered for re-pointing; edit that entry by hand. One whose `frameworkRange` excludes the linked
     framework shows an advisory line and can still be added. Offers are not rows — Doctor check 16
     never reports them.
   - **Add a catalog offer** — with the framework **pinned by git** at an immutable ref (its entry has
     `?path=/Packages/com.classicspins.prototype-framework` and a `#v<semver>` tag or a full 40-hex
     commit), the Wizard reads `Editor/Modules/modules.catalog.json` from the resolved framework (a git
     package brings only the framework's folder, so the catalog is how it knows its siblings) and offers
     every entry not registered and not `withheld`, sourced **"From the framework's catalog at
     `<ref>`"**. **Add** writes the framework's own entry text with **only the `?path=` value swapped**
     for the entry's `path` — same host, same credentials, same `#ref`, its leading/trailing `/` style
     kept. The module comes from the commit the framework's release gate checked it at. A manifest
     that already declares the module is a rejected offer, as above. Pinned at a **branch** or with no
     `#ref`, nothing is offered and one Modules line says to pin a `v<semver>` tag or a full commit (UPM
     locks each git package separately, so a branch could hand the module a different commit). A
     framework tag older than the catalog (`v0.8.3` and earlier) has no file: nothing is offered and nothing is said.
   - A **registered** package the linked checkout or the catalog names as a module, whose own root has
     no `pf-module.json`, shows as a **rejection row** in the Wizard and in Doctor check 16.
   - An Add that reports **"did not take"** wrote nothing you can trust: read the written entry in
     `Packages/manifest.json` and UPM's message in the Console, then fix the entry by hand.
   - **Add by git URL** — paste the module's URL into the Modules section. The door for every other
     case: a framework pinned by registry or tarball, or embedded, offers nothing, and neither does a
     module from another repository. The URL is the module's `source` (its own `<slug>/v*` tag).
2. **Install** on that row — writes only scoped registries and registry dependencies into
   `Packages/manifest.json` (nothing else: no scene, prefab or asset). Refused, with the reason, on a
   `framework-range:`, `conflict:` or `seam:` fact.
3. **Checklist** — `manualSteps` verbatim, the installer's `menu` path and the substituted
   `assetPath`. **`Framework/Modules/Create Installer Assets`** creates the empty installer asset at that
   path for every module still missing one (confirm dialog, never overwrites, never touches a scene —
   the one asset write the module tooling makes, FR18 amended 2026-10-13). Dropping it into
   `RootLifetimeScope`'s game-installer slot in the Master Scene stays **human zone** (rule #12) — a
   live editor, never YAML.

**Doctor check 16** renders the same state list: `Ready`, `Partial` with every missing fact by name
(`registry:`, `scope:`, `package:`, `assembly:`, `define:`, `installer-asset`, `sku`, `framework-range:`,
`conflict:`, `seam:`), or `Absent`. It **reports and never blocks**. In the framework repo, which
installs no SDK, `pf-ads-max` correctly reads `Partial`.

## 11. Distribution

A module is distributed the way the framework is: git URL
`…?path=/Packages/com.classicspins.pf-<domain>#<slug>/v<version>`. Git tags are repo-global, so a
module tags **`<slug>/v<version>`** (e.g. `ads-max/v0.1.0`); a bare `v<version>` is the framework's
alone. Before a module tag, the framework's own release gates run green (`AGENTS.framework.md` §5c).

## 12. Gate

```sh
cd HeadlessTests && dotnet test              # framework-pure ship gate (module core, drift-gate logic)
sh Tools/CI/module-tests.sh                  # every module's Tests~/*HeadlessTests — CI step 5c
sh Tools/CI/greps.sh source                  # incl. buildhook + modulegate: no build hook, no BootNodeOverride.Gate( in a module
Tools/Build/pf-build.sh modules --check      # pf-module.json vs the module's code — CI step 3 drift gate
```

- **`modules --check`** holds the metadata true: `define` ↔ the gated asmdef (and the marker),
  `installer.type` ↔ an `IInstaller` class in the ungated runtime role, `port.interface` and every
  `ports[i].interface` ↔ an interface in the API index (a `ports[]` entry that repeats `port.interface`
  or an earlier entry is drift too), `id` ↔ `package.json`. **The catalog leg** holds
  `Packages/com.classicspins.prototype-framework/Editor/Modules/modules.catalog.json` (`pf-catalog/1`)
  true too: every entry's `<path>/pf-module.json` exists with the same `id`, `displayName` and
  `summary`, and its `frameworkRange` admits the framework `package.json` version; **every in-repo
  module is an entry or `withheld`**, and every withheld id is an in-repo module. **A new module adds
  its catalog entry** (or a `withheld` id until it is releasable) in the same change — otherwise step 3
  is red naming it. Exit `0` ok · `1` drift (each line names the module and the field) ·
  `2` a file it cannot read. It sees only modules **inside this repo** — a registry-resolved module in
  a consumer's `Library/PackageCache/` is Doctor check 16's, advisory.
- **5c** globs `Runtime/Core/**` only, so it runs with no SDK installed. Adding a module parameterises
  5c — it never adds a CI step.
- **EditMode** through `Tools/pf/pf-tests <Classes>` only when the module's `Editor` role (or the
  framework's module editor code) changed. Never batchmode locally.
- **One boot smoke** (`pf-gates` has the procedure) for the wiring: an installer registration is only
  provable at runtime — boot once and confirm the resolved implementation is yours and the refusal
  line names your module when the SDK is absent.
- **Say what you skipped**, one line each. The PlayMode suite is CI's. A real ad, and the SDK's
  consent flow, are proven only on a device in a consumer project — the in-editor SDK stub proves
  nothing; report them **unverified**.

## 13. A tool module — `pf-module/2`, `kind: tool` (AD-MOD-14, AD-MOD-15)

A **tool** is a module that adds **editor or command-line capability** to a consumer — a release build
pipeline, an importer, a generator — and **borrows no runtime seam**: no port, no installer slot, no boot
node, nothing in a player. The first one is `pf-build-tools` (signed iOS `.ipa` / Android `.aab` builds).
It is still a module: one self-description, one discovery (Setup Wizard ▸ Modules, Doctor check 16), one
install door, one gate set — each branching on `kind`, never on a module's name.

### The two schema majors

| File | Kind | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `pf-module/1` | always `service` | Valid forever; **a new service keeps writing `/1`**. A `kind` key in a `/1` file is refused, naming `kind` and its value. |
| `pf-module/2` | `kind` **required**, closed at `service` \| `tool` | A `/2` service reads exactly like `/1`. A missing or unknown `kind` is one rejection naming it; a new kind is a spine change. `pf-module/3` is refused as an unknown major. |

A `/2` file's `frameworkRange` must admit **no framework below 0.8.6** (`ModuleMetadata.ToolSchemaFloor`,
the first release whose reader understands `/2` — an older one rejects the file as an unknown major).
`modules --check` names `frameworkRange` otherwise.

### Fields

```jsonc
{
  "schema": "pf-module/2",
  "kind": "tool",
  "id": "com.classicspins.pf-build-tools",           // == package.json "name"
  "displayName": "Build Tools — signed iOS / Android release builds",
  "summary": "… Delete Assets/BuildTools (the old .unitypackage copy) before adding this module.",
  "frameworkRange": ">=0.8.6 <0.9.0",                // bound: capped at the next minor · free: open, >=0.8.6
  "source": { "kind": "git", "url": "…?path=/Packages/com.classicspins.pf-build-tools#build-tools/v0.1.0" },
  "requires": { "scopedRegistries": [], "dependencies": {} },   // REQUIRED and EMPTY
  "manualSteps": [ "Export the signing environment variables …", "…" ],
  "docs": "recipes/add-service-module.md"
}
```

**Forbidden for a tool: `port`, `ports`, `define`, `installer`** — present at all (even `null`), each is
one rejection naming it. Faking one to satisfy the reader would make the drift gate check fiction. A
non-empty `requires.scopedRegistries`, `requires.dependencies`, `requires.manualPackages` or
`requires.manualAssemblies` is refused by name: a tool that needs a
package is service-shaped, or routed.

### Layout — two roles, both editor-only

```
Packages/com.classicspins.pf-<tool>/
├── package.json · pf-module.json        pf-module/2, kind: tool
├── Editor/        ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.<Tool>.Editor   REQUIRED: menus, windows, parameterless -executeMethod doors
├── Editor/Core/   ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.<Tool>.Core     optional: engine-free pure logic
├── <Payload>~/    non-C# payload (Shell~/, templates) — found via PackageInfo.FindForAssembly
└── Tests~/<Tool>HeadlessTests/          globs Editor/Core/**; may run the payload's own suite — CI step 5c
```

- **Every tool asmdef is `includePlatforms: ["Editor"]` and has no `defineConstraints`** — a tool compiles
  nothing into a player and is never gated. `…Core` also sets `noEngineReferences: true`. No `Sdk` or
  runtime role, no marker, no installer.
- **Framework-free or framework-bound, never in between.** *Free*: no framework assembly referenced, no
  framework dependency in `package.json`, an open range `>=0.8.6`. *Bound*: `Editor` references
  `ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Editor` (and `Core` may reference `CS.PF.{Domain, Application}` and
  UniTask); `package.json` pins the framework **exactly at its version**, like a service; the range is
  **capped at the next minor**, because editor types are not in the API index. Never `Presentation`,
  `Views`, `Infrastructure`, `Composition`, `Game.*` or a third-party SDK.
- **Naming** — id `com.classicspins.pf-<slug>`, assemblies by the id→name rule (`pf-build-tools` ⇒
  `ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Build.Tools.{Editor, Core}`), namespace ≡ assembly, tag
  `<slug>/v<version>`. Slugs `domain`, `application`, `presentation`, `views`, `infrastructure`,
  `composition`, `editor` and `tests` are **reserved** (either kind — `modules --check` names `id`).
- **Payload** — a script **never derives the project from its own location** (under a dev-linked
  framework that walk finds the framework checkout, itself a Unity project): the project root is a
  required argument or environment variable the C# side or the CI step sets. Scripts run through an
  interpreter (`bash <file>`), write only under the project's output folders or `$TMPDIR`, and are
  reached from outside Unity through a Unity `-executeMethod` door — never a literal
  `Library/PackageCache` path.
- **Superseding a pre-module copy** — the README and `summary` say to delete the old copy **before**
  adding the module (duplicate GUIDs otherwise); the Editor role refuses with a named error when a second
  definition of its entry type is loaded; script `.meta` GUIDs are kept so existing assets rebind.

### A tool that drives a build (AD-MOD-15)

- **Success is the report's**: delete the export location first; exit `0` only when
  `report.summary.result` is `Succeeded` with zero errors; the `-executeMethod` door is parameterless,
  `try/catch → Exit(2)`, and calls `Exit` only under batchmode; packaging/upload run only after exit `0`
  in the same run (a marker written in that run, never "the folder exists").
- **One player per project**: set every build setting explicitly per build and restore it in a
  `finally`; build Addressables content through the framework's one door,
  **`BuildEntry.RunContentBuild(BuildTarget)`** — never the active target or a command-line default.
- **Secrets** come only from the process environment: never a serialized object (`ScriptableObject`,
  `ProjectSettings`, `EditorPrefs`), never argv, never echoed, never in an artifact. Identifiers and
  key-file paths are not secrets. `manualSteps` name the environment variables and the consumer
  `.gitignore` lines.
- **Never run by an agent locally**: the batchmode launcher refuses on `Temp/UnityLockfile` with exit `2`.
  A tool build is CI's or a human's, like `pf-build.sh player`.
- **Post-build transforms only** (AD-MOD-6): an `Info.plist` key or a Gradle property, with an explicit
  order, never overwriting a different existing value — log the module, the key and both values and keep
  the existing one.

### State, Wizard and Doctor

A tool's facts are only **`package:`** and **`framework-range:`**. It reads **`Ready`** when resolved and
in range; there is nothing to Install (its `requires` is empty, so the Wizard shows no Install), no
installer asset to create (`Create Installer Assets` skips it), and its **checklist is its `manualSteps`
alone**.

### Gate

The same commands as §12. `modules --check` runs the **tool leg** instead of the define / installer / port
checks: role folders, editor-only asmdefs without `defineConstraints`, `noEngineReferences` on `Core`, the
free-or-bound edge set, the exact framework pin and the next-minor cap, the `/2` floor and the reserved
slugs. `AssemblyGraphTests` pins every tool asmdef's edges like a service's. A tool with a `Core` **or** a
payload suite ships `Tests~/<Tool>HeadlessTests` (step 5c); its payload suite runs **as a case in it**
under a scrubbed environment — **never a new CI step**.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| The fake still runs | The installer asset is not in the Master Scene slot, or the installer assembly was gated so the asset is a missing script (§4). |
| Safe Mode after switching branches or deleting an SDK outside Unity | Remove the declared manual SDK symbol in Player Settings for every installed target, then restore/import the SDK (§3a). |
| Every ad call fails and logs your module id | `Null<Sdk>Bridge` — the define is not armed. Doctor check 16 names the `define:` or `package:` fact; run Install. |
| Doctor shows `define:` although the SDK package resolved | The marker type is missing from the `Sdk` role, or `versionDefines` names another package/version (§2). |
| `modules --check` reports `define` | `pf-module.json` `define` no longer matches the gated asmdef's `defineConstraints`/`versionDefines`, or the marker was renamed. |
| `modules --check` reports `installer.type` | The class was renamed, moved to another namespace, lost `IInstaller`, or sits in the gated role. |
| `modules --check` reports `id` | `pf-module.json` `id` ≠ `package.json` `name` — the Wizard and Doctor would read the module as `Absent`. |
| The build fails with a `BuildFailedException` listing `[<module id>]` lines | Your `IModulePreflight` found a half-wired install — each line says what to fix. |
| `greps.sh source` fails `buildhook` | The module implements a forbidden build callback (a preprocessor, scene / assembly / linker / shader processor); move the check into `IModulePreflight` (§8) — only post-build transforms are permitted. |
| `modules --check` names `kind`, `port`, `ports`, `define` or `installer` on a tool | A `pf-module/2` file without a valid `kind`, or a tool carrying a forbidden field (§13). |
| `modules --check` names `frameworkRange` or `package.json` on a tool | The range admits a framework below 0.8.6, a bound tool is not capped at the next minor or not pinned exactly at the framework version, or a free tool declares the framework (§13). |
| `modules --check` names `asmdef.*` on a tool | An asmdef outside `Editor/` / `Editor/Core/`, not editor-only, define-gated, a `Core` without `noEngineReferences`, or a reference outside the free-or-bound edge set (§13). |
| `greps.sh source` fails `modulegate` | Module code calls `BootNodeOverride.Gate(` — gating is SKU composition only (AD-MOD-3). Delete it; the SKU gates your node. A headless test under `Tests~/` may compose one. |
| `modules --check` reports `ports[i].interface` | The interface is not in the API index, is not an interface, or repeats `port.interface` / an earlier entry. |
| Input stays locked / audio stays ducked / the sim never resumes after an ad or the consent prompt | The closing `AdVisibilityChanged(false)` was not published in a `finally` on every exit path. |
| A privacy prompt disappears mid-read, or ads go offline after an unrelated consent change | A timeout over the interactive flow, or init not memoized per process (§7). |
| A deep link or consent rerun silently does nothing | A replaced boot node changed its `Id` or `Provides` (§6). |
| "Privacy settings" opens nothing on device, or the row never draws although the module is installed | The SKU registered `IAdsPrivacyOptions` itself (a fake, or an `IConsentService` wrapper): SKU installers run last, so it shadows the module's replacement — two registrants of one `replacement` port, the same clash `seam:` names between modules. Delete the SKU registration and consume the port (§5). |
| `VContainerException` naming a parameter you thought was optional | A defaulted constructor parameter (§9). |
| `type or namespace <Sdk> not found` in a SKU | A SKU assembly referencing the SDK — only the module's `Sdk` role may. |
